headline: War Premium Grips Markets as Mideast Turmoil Tilts Thursday's Session
body_html:
Thursday's session closed with the S&P 500 slipping modestly lower, as geopolitical anxiety anchored sentiment throughout the day. Reports of Houthi missile strikes on Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu, paired with the U.S. Senate's rejection of a resolution to limit the executive's Iran war powers, kept investors cautious. Breadth told a clear story: 326 names in our 545-stock universe finished in the red against just 218 gainers.

The dominant rotation was unmistakable — money moved toward defensively oriented healthcare names and away from rate-sensitive cyclicals. Healthcare led all sectors, gaining 0.27%, while Homebuilders added 0.16% and Energy edged up 0.10%. On the other side of the ledger, Materials shed 1.20%, Semiconductors dropped 0.96%, and Industrials fell 0.90%, reflecting broad risk-off repositioning as Hormuz-corridor concerns weighed on global-growth proxies.

The session's standout mover was Everpure (ticker: P), which surged 11.15% to lead all gainers — a striking divergence from the prevailing cautious tone. Healthcare diagnostics names Veracyte and NeoGenomics also posted double-digit and near-double-digit gains respectively, underscoring the sector's defensive appeal on a day when geopolitical headlines dominated the tape.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strikes on Saudi Oil Infrastructure Rattle Energy Markets
briefs.body: The Houthi movement claimed responsibility for attacks on Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu on Thursday, with Saudi authorities confirming they intercepted incoming missiles. Red Sea insurance premiums for Saudi oil exports were already climbing before the strikes, and the combination threatens to add a meaningful logistical surcharge to the kingdom's export strategy.

briefs.headline: Senate Leaves Trump's Iran War Authority Intact
briefs.body: A Democratic-led resolution seeking to curtail the administration's Iran war powers was defeated in the U.S. Senate on Thursday, leaving the executive with broad latitude over military posture in the region. Markets interpreted the vote as a signal that the current confrontational stance toward Tehran is unlikely to soften in the near term, sustaining the geopolitical risk premium.

briefs.headline: Acadia Pharmaceuticals Tumbles Nearly 13%, Leading Decliners
briefs.body: Acadia Pharmaceuticals finished as the session's sharpest loser, shedding 12.78% by the close. The biotech's steep drop stood out even in a broadly weak tape, suggesting company-specific catalysts drove the selling. First Solar was close behind, falling 10.32% as solar names faced a difficult session alongside broader cyclical weakness.

briefs.headline: Arm Holdings Slides as Semiconductor Sector Faces Broad Pressure
briefs.body: Chip-architecture licensor Arm Holdings fell 7.88%, contributing to a 0.96% sector-wide decline in semiconductors — one of Thursday's worst-performing groups. The move reflects growing investor unease about global-growth durability amid rising rates and Mideast supply-chain risk, with the semiconductor complex serving as a reliable barometer of that anxiety.

briefs.headline: US-Iran Hormuz Talks Emerge Quietly Amid War Drumbeats
briefs.body: Even as military tensions escalated, sources told Reuters that U.S. and Iranian officials have been discussing a phased arrangement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and wind down the American blockade. The parallel diplomatic track introduced a note of ambiguity for energy traders, tempering what might otherwise have been a sharper spike in risk premiums.

briefs.headline: Rising-Rate History Casts Shadow Over Session's Undercurrent
briefs.body: Beyond the headlines, a quieter concern circulated among fixed-income watchers Thursday: historical precedent suggests that sharp, rapid interest-rate increases tend to precede financial system stress, with analysts warning that something typically breaks when the pace of tightening reaches current levels. That backdrop added a layer of unease beneath the geopolitical noise driving the session.
